## Limitations and future work {#sec-limitations}

- "Reality" is ComFree with 71 perturbed parameters, so the sim-to-real gap SysID closes is purely parametric; there is no real robot. <!-- F:T7 -->
- SysID uses batched central finite differences, not gradients through the simulator. <!-- F:S1 -->
- Repetitions are same-seed reruns on a non-deterministic simulator, with n = 3 and 16 episodes per evaluation. <!-- F:C1 -->
- 3 of 78 runs are degenerate for reasons I did not investigate. <!-- F:R10 -->
- The planner was still improving at 300k steps, so no configuration is converged. <!-- F:R9 --> <!-- F:R22 -->
- The drift-ratio diagnostics come from one run per configuration. <!-- F:R14 -->
- The TD-MPC2 baseline is a single run with different hyperparameters and no terminal masking. <!-- F:B3 -->
- The learned reward head is trained but never used.  <!-- F:M4 -->

<!-- FALLBACK:sim2sim (once sim2sim results exist: delete this block and re-add the sim2sim include in index.qmd) -->
**A different contact model.** The obvious next test changes what SysID cannot fix: the contact model. I built an evaluation that runs the trained agents in stock CPU MuJoCo [@todorov2012mujoco] on the same scene, parameters and task code, with only the contact solver changed (parameter parity checked to about 1e-7 relative error). The planner keeps planning through ComFree, synced to the MuJoCo state. Running it on the well-trained runs is the first item of future work. <!-- F:X1 --> <!-- F:X2 --> <!-- F:X3 -->
<!-- /FALLBACK -->

**Future work.** Move to a real Allegro hand [@allegrohand], where the gap is no longer only parametric. Restrict SysID to the parameters short chunks can observe. Close the policy–planner gap, which none of my interventions did.
